newsitem.title: UK: Too early to say strong stg hurting UK exports - CBI.
newsitem.headline: Too early to say strong stg hurting UK exports - CBI.

text.p: UK exporters have not yet felt the pinch of sterling's recent strength, the Confederation of British Industry said on Thursday.
"At the moment it is too early to say whether it's a problem or not," Sudhir Junankar, the CBI's associate director of economic analysis, said at a press conference.

The pound jumped above 2.40 marks on Thursday for the first time since early 1995. It has gained nearly four percent against the mark in the past month and just over two percent on a trade-weighted basis.
By 1110 GMT, it was trading at 2.3985/90 marks.
Junankar said the CBI's next industrial trends survey, due later this month, would give a better clue to exporters' concerns, or lack of them, about the pound's strength.
"So far, we haven't picked up any worsening of the situation, but the next survey will ask whether there are price constraints on exports," he said. "That's really a proxy for the exchange rate."
Junankar said that in general, UK exporters were more concerned about the prospects for economic recovery in key European markets. "The exchange rate is just one element of the story."
He said British companies were not overly worried by short-term currency movements. "If the pound's strength is sustained, then it could become more of a problem."
